_source: India Meteorological Department (IMD) / Regional Specialized Meteorological Centre (RSMC) New Delhi - Tropical Cyclone Landfall Climatology (https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/landfall.php)
_climatology_summary: Over 60% of Bay of Bengal tropical cyclones make landfall on India's East Coast, with two distinct seasons: pre-monsoon (April-June) and post-monsoon (October-December), with October-December being the primary and most active season. Climatological peak landfall timing: Odisha & West Bengal coasts peak in October; Andhra Pradesh coast peaks in November; Tamil Nadu coast peaks in December.

Odisha.climatology_note: Odisha coast landfall frequency peaks in October during the post-monsoon cyclone season (Oct-Dec) with secondary pre-monsoon activity (Apr-Jun).

West Bengal.climatology_note: West Bengal / Sundarbans coast landfall frequency peaks in October during post-monsoon season.

Andhra Pradesh.climatology_note: Andhra Pradesh coast landfall frequency peaks in November during the post-monsoon cyclone season.

Tamil Nadu.climatology_note: Tamil Nadu coast landfall frequency peaks in December during the late post-monsoon / northeast monsoon season.
